reason: Verified in source and in the live render, not inferred. b.css .b-edit (line 387) declares `background: var(--back)` at line 390 and `background: var(--fore-06)` at line 395 in the same block; the later declaration wins and getComputedStyle in Chromium returns backgroundColor rgba(255,255,255,0.06), backgroundImage none. .b-item is position:absolute (b.css:152), so at 1440x960 on state=owner-editing the plate rect is 734,656 to 1254,993 and exactly three absolutely-positioned non-editing items sit inside it: Final dress fitting (761-840), Choose the evening music (859-938), Final guest numbers (957-1036). A clipped screenshot of the plate confirms the double-print visually: 'Final dress fitting' prints across the WHEN label, the -7 and -1 steppers sit on top of 'SAT 22 AUG', and 'Choose the evening music' crosses the visibility row. This is the primary gesture of the direction, illegible in the one state built to demonstrate it, and the rule's own comment ('It gets an opaque ground so nothing reads through') proves the intent was already the opposite. Neither gate sees it: audit.mjs composites background-color up the ancestor chain for contrast and has no z-order or overlap test, and interaction-check.mjs asserts only that the stepper moves the edited item and nothing else. Not taste, not a gate restatement, no constraint touched.
sharpenedFix: Take the first half of the proposed fix, drop the second. (1) In .b-edit collapse the two background declarations into one opaque plate that keeps the identical tint and introduces no new declared colour: `background: linear-gradient(var(--fore-06), var(--fore-06)), var(--back);` — or, preferable for gate honesty, keep `background: var(--back);` as the only background-color and paint the tint with `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 100vmax var(--fore-06);`, because audit.mjs's backdropOf() stops at the first opaque background-color and would otherwise judge the plate's own text against the page ground rather than the tinted plate. (2) Do NOT add the blanket `.b-measure[data-editing="true"] .b-item:not([data-editing="true"]) { opacity: 0.28; pointer-events: none; }`. With an opaque plate the three intersecting rows are fully covered edge to edge (plate 734-1254 spans the same column as the items), so the dim is invisible exactly where the finding says it is needed, and everywhere else it is a net loss: element opacity is invisible to audit.mjs's contrast pass, so 0.28 on --fore-72 text would silently ship roughly 2:1 body text past a gate that is meant to guard AA; it also dims every tick, anchor marker and away-count on the measure the direction is built around, and pointer-events:none kills click-to-edit-another-item in the real build (the lab has no such handler yet, so the regression would land unnoticed here). If the occlusion still needs stating, state it on the plate itself — e.g. a single mono hairline count on the plate's lower edge naming how many dates it is covering — rather than by draining ink from the measure. Item top positions stay untouched either way.
